milestone: M59 Budgeted Product Continuation Drive Loop

strategic_capability_mapping.relationship: Moves product-continuation looping from caller choreography into a bounded Rust-owned drive sequence.
Lets the explicit loop advance multiple eligible product-continuation route steps through existing continuation/task-run authority.
Revalidates route kind, checkpoint freshness, and replay identity before each derived route step.

answers.strategic_capabilities: Advances headless_autonomous_development with agent_loop, runtime_permission_enforcement, and persistent_structured_ledger support.
answers.new_capability: One headless.run.drive request can execute a bounded sequence of runtime-derived product-continuation route steps.
answers.why_existing_functionality_is_insufficie: M58.2 derived only one product-continuation target per request; later route decisions still required caller-side looping.
answers.product_gap_if_skipped: Scheduled callers still need external glue for multi-step product-continuation progress and cannot replay one bounded runtime-owned sequence result.
answers.non_duplicative: Distinct from M57 admission/run and M58 explicit/derived one-step drive because this phase sequences existing derived advances across route changes.
answers.no_new_rpc: Yes. The existing headless.run.drive surface is extended; no JSON-RPC method is added.
answers.no_new_summary: Yes. The existing bounded drive result carries advances, stop reason, replay status, next route, and fingerprint.
answers.runtime_behavior_change: The drive loop reuses product_continuation_derived_target after the first advance when the latest persisted route remains product-continuation, and stops closed otherwise.
answers.headless_autonomous_contribution: A headless controller can delegate a small product-continuation sequence to Rust runtime authority instead of deciding every next request externally.
answers.milestone_progress: Implements the core M59 transition from one-step derived execution to budgeted derived sequence execution.

exit_criteria: headless.run.drive can execute at least two eligible product_continuation_derived_target route advances in one bounded request
the runtime re-reads the latest session checkpoint between derived product-continuation advances
the sequence stops closed when the latest route is not a product-continuation route
exact replay returns the persisted drive sequence without duplicate TaskRunning or continuation decision evidence
behavior tests cover multi-advance derived sequence execution and mismatched replay denial
no new JSON-RPC method, report, digest, history, readiness, verdict, preview, inspection, dashboard, provider expansion, workspace mutation expansion, or VSIX-owned policy is introduced

ledger and RPC outputs exclude raw prompts, provider responses, file content, diffs, stdout/stderr, commands, environment values, raw requests, raw ledger payloads, absolute paths, canonical paths, tokens, and secrets

behavior_evidence: multi-advance derived product-continuation drive behavior test
safety_boundary: one derived target reused only while latest route is product-continuation
checkpoint re-read before subsequent derived advance
exact replay validates subordinate request identity
non_goals: no unbounded loop or background scheduler
technical_debt: runtime lib.rs remains large; split only through later behavior-preserving refactor
next_capability_rationale: If accepted, M59 can close out unless sequence interruption needs a distinct recovery route.

guard_engine_change_review.review_intent: M59.1 updates current and archived phase-value manifests for a runtime behavior phase. Review must confirm guard enforcement is not weakened and no wrapper/report/readiness surface was added.
